title: Claude Helps Solve First 3D Structure of a Prokaryotic Vault Particle
whyItMatters: A small team with limited structural-biology background used Claude to solve the first 3D structure of a microbial vault particle—a 40-year cell-biology mystery—in under four months.
summary: Vaults are enigmatic hollow protein barrels discovered in 1986 whose biological purpose remains unknown. Working with Claude across protocol design, troubleshooting, and cryo-EM reconstruction, Anthropic’s biology lab resolved the first 3D structure of a prokaryotic/phage vault particle (phage L05, built from 96 protein copies vs. 78 in human vaults), compressing a 3-day purification protocol to 90 minutes and producing an initial structural model in 34 hours.
technicalHighlights: Resolved the first 3D cryo-EM structure of a non-eukaryotic vault particle (96-subunit hollow barrel with three-tiered tapered cap).
Compressed protein purification from 3 days to ~90 minutes and initial 3D structural modeling from weeks to 34 hours.
Published candid error logs alongside the bioRxiv preprint—documenting a 2-week growth-medium error and mirror-image map caught by humans.
caveats: Determines the 3D molecular structure rather than the biological function of vault particles; submitted as a bioRxiv preprint awaiting peer review.

scoreRationale.foundational: First 3D structural determination of a prokaryotic vault particle after four decades of open mystery.
scoreRationale.ripple: Proved generalist AI assistants can empower non-specialist wet-lab teams to execute cryo-EM structural biology.
scoreRationale.verification: Experimental cryo-EM structural data submitted to bioRxiv with transparent failure/correction documentation.
scoreRationale.velocity: Completed an end-to-end structural biology project from scratch in under four months.
